row: FARFIELD BC-VARIATION PROBE on the L1 loaded arm. Mesh mesh_L1_A1 (31,752 cells, 5-degree wedge), delta_p = 1000 Pa, U_inf = 20 m/s, simpleFoam steady incompressible kOmegaSST low-Re, OpenFOAM v2606, 4 ranks, 15000-iteration rigor cap. THE SINGLE VARIATION: the farfield patch becomes `slip` on U, p, k, omega and nut. Nothing else changes.
hypothesis_under_test: The farfield patch carries p: totalPressure p0=0 with U: inletOutlet inletValue (20 0 0). On a boundary whose normal is radial, a forced axial inflow has a near-zero normal component while the pressure form lets the outer boundary pass mass freely, so THE MASS FLUX THROUGH THE OUTER BOUNDARY IS A FREE PARAMETER THE SIMPLE LOOP NEVER SETTLES. Measured support at dp=0: 41.38 % of `sum local` continuity error on the 256 farfield-adjacent cells, 59.63 % in the outer radial band r in [3.0, 3.577). `slip` sets the boundary-normal flux identically to zero, removing exactly that degree of freedom and nothing else.
stated_limitation: REGISTERED IN ADVANCE, IN THE PRE-COMMITTED FILE: `slip` confines the flow and is NOT proposed as the production farfield. This probe identifies a MECHANISM; it does not select a boundary condition. If it confirms, the production form is a separate question and its choice is the supervisor's.

retry_note: RETRY ON A MEASURED DEFECT IN THIS LANE'S OWN LAUNCHER, AT ZERO COMPUTE SPENT. The first attempt (queued 2026-08-31T19:48Z) ABORTED at phase=guards with launcher_rc=1 and solver_rc=not-run; nothing was decomposed, no processor* directory was created, no field was written and NOTHING WAS DELETED. Cause: run_f28_bcprobe.sh inherited its time-directory guard verbatim from run_f28_feasibility.sh as `.*/[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$`, where it is CORRECT because that script assembles into an empty directory and any `0` it finds is somebody else's answer. HERE `0` IS AN INPUT -- the probe case is pre-assembled and its initial condition is the thing under test -- so the inherited guard refused the only directory it was ever meant to run. THE GUARD DID ITS JOB: it refused rather than running, and it cost nothing to be wrong. The repair adds `-not -name '0'`, excluding EXACTLY the literal `0` and nothing else, and IT WAS DRIVEN IN SIX DIRECTIONS BEFORE THIS ENTRY WAS RE-QUEUED (standing rule 3): the real probe dir and a bare 0-only tree both pass; planted `15000`, `0.0`, `00` and `1` directories each still abort, as does the parent arm's real `14000` answer directory. The guard is NARROWED BY ONE EXACT NAME, NOT WEAKENED. This is the same lesson the first attempt's checker taught an hour earlier from the other side: a guard copied from a script whose preconditions differ is a guard aimed at something other than what it thinks.
